verdict.rationale: MoQ documents its own way to send arbitrary low-latency data alongside media. Chat, game state, telemetry and control channels run over the same relays through the moq-net and @moq/net libraries, and custom tracks can carry any live content. The GitHub README treats text chat as a core feature and claims WebRTC-like latency. However, the pack only links to the data API pages without showing their content, and nothing shows data being synchronized with audio and video within a participant session. missing for 10: published data-API reference details (message semantics, ordering and reliability options), evidence of data tracks tied to a session alongside audio and video, independent or hands-on corroboration of data-channel use.

support.subject: As a developer, participants exchange low-latency arbitrary data in the session alongside audio and video, with a documented data API

citations.quote: Chat, game state, telemetry, and control channels over the same relays with [`moq-net`](/lib/rs/moq-net.html) or [`@moq/net`](/lib/js/net.html).
Extend the protocol with custom tracks for any live content.
Includes text chat as both an example and a core feature.
MoQ delivers WebRTC-like latency without the constraints of WebRTC.
